Vālmiki.description: The legendary sage and author of the Ramayana, depicted as an ascetic and poet who composes the epic after being inspired by the gods.

Nārada.description: A divine sage known for his knowledge of the three worlds and his role as a messenger and advisor among gods and humans.

Ikshwāku.description: The founder of the Ikshwāku dynasty, the royal lineage to which Rāma belongs.

Rāma.description: The hero of the Ramayana and eldest son of Daçarātha, he is an incarnation of Vishnu and a descendant of the Raghu and Kakutstha lineages.

Vishnu.description: One of the principal Hindu deities and preserver of the universe who incarnates as Rāma to defeat evil.

Himavat.description: The personification of the Himalaya mountains, often referenced for his patience and grandeur.

Daçarātha.description: The righteous King of Ayodhyā and father of Rāma, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Satrughna.

Kaikeyi.description: One of Daçarātha's queens, mother of Bharata, whose request leads to Rāma's exile.

Bharata.description: Son of Daçarātha and Kaikeyi, younger brother of Rāma, known for his devotion to Rāma and refusal to accept the throne.

Lakshmana.description: Son of Daçarātha and Sumitrā, devoted brother and companion of Rāma.

Rohini.description: A star or celestial figure, here used in simile to describe Sita's devotion to Rāma.

Janaka.description: King of Mithilā, father of Sita, known for his wisdom and righteousness; Videha is his kingdom.

Sitā.description: Daughter of Janaka and wife of Rāma, she is an incarnation of divine power and the ideal of womanly virtue.

Guha.description: King of the Nishādas, a tribal chief who befriends and assists Rāma during his exile; associated with the region/city Sringaverapura.

Chitrakuta.description: A forested mountain region where Rāma, Sita, and Lakshmana reside during exile.

Brāhmanas.description: Members of the priestly class, often depicted as learned, virtuous, and engaged in sacred duties.

Rākshasa.description: A class or race of demons or night-rangers, often antagonists in the Ramayana; female Rakshasas are called Rākshasi.

Virādha.description: A Rākshasa slain by Rāma in the Dandaka forest.

Sarabhanga.description: A sage encountered by Rāma during his exile.

Agastya.description: A powerful sage who aids Rāma and gives him divine weapons.

Surpanakhā.description: A Rākshasi (female demon), sister of Rāvana, whose actions lead to the main conflict.

Khara.description: A Rākshasa, brother of Surpanakhā, slain by Rāma.

Tricira.description: A Rākshasa, ally of Khara, slain by Rāma.

Dushana.description: A Rākshasa, another ally of Khara, slain by Rāma.

Rāvana.description: The ten-headed king of Lankā, chief antagonist of the Ramayana, abductor of Sita.

Māricha.description: A Rākshasa who assists Rāvana in abducting Sita.

Jatāyu.description: A vulture who tries to rescue Sita from Rāvana and is mortally wounded.

Savari.description: A female ascetic who offers hospitality and guidance to Rāma.

Hanumān.description: The monkey-god, son of the Wind god, devoted servant of Rāma, famed for his strength and loyalty.

Sugriva.description: King of the monkeys, ally of Rāma, aided by Hanumān.

Vāli.description: Brother of Sugriva, a powerful monkey king slain by Rāma.

Sampāti.description: A vulture king and brother of Jatāyu who helps the monkeys locate Sitā in Lankā.

Aksha.description: A son of Rāvana, slain by Hanumān in Lankā.

Indrajit.description: The powerful son of Rāvana and Mandodari who famously bound Hanumān.

Nala.description: A monkey chief who constructs the bridge to Lankā.

Pushpaka.description: A magical aerial chariot used by Rāma to return to Ayodhyā.

Kusi.description: One of Rāma and Sita's twin sons, raised in Vālmiki's hermitage.

Lava.description: The other twin son of Rāma and Sita, also raised by Vālmiki.

Brahmā.description: The creator god and lord of creatures, often identified as the progenitor of the universe.

Manu.description: The progenitor of mankind and founder of Ayodhyā.

Sagara.description: A legendary king, ancestor of Rāma, famed for digging the ocean.

Sataghnis.description: War machines or weapons used for defense.

Athiratha.description: A title meaning a great chariot-warrior.

Romapāda.description: King of the Angas, friend of Daçarātha.

Sanat Kumāra.description: A divine sage, son of Brahmā, known for prophecy.

Rhishyasringa.description: A sage with mystical powers, son-in-law of Daçarātha, who performs the sacrifice for sons.

Sāntā.description: Daughter of Romapāda, wife of Rhishyasringa.

Jāvāli.description: A Brāhmana and priest in Ayodhyā known for his skeptical views.

Sumantra.description: Chief minister and charioteer of Daçarātha.

Kosala.description: The kingdom ruled by Daçarātha, with Ayodhyā as its capital.

Sarayu.description: A sacred river flowing by Ayodhyā.

Vedāngas.description: Ancillary disciplines associated with the study and understanding of the Vedas.

Golden age.description: A mythological era of prosperity and virtue, often referenced as an ideal time.

Brāhmana.description: A member of the priestly caste in Hindu society.

Kshatriya.description: The warrior and ruling caste/class in Hindu society.

Vaisya.description: The merchant and agricultural caste in Hindu society.

Sudra.description: The laborer and service-providing caste in Hindu society.

Tamasā.description: A river near which Vālmiki's hermitage is situated.

Rāmāyana.description: The epic poem composed by Vālmiki, narrating the story of Rāma.

yoga.description: A spiritual and meditative discipline for self-realization.

Viswāmitra.description: A renowned sage, formerly a king, who attained Brahmarshi status and plays a key role in Rāma's early adventures.

Parasurāma.description: An avatar of Vishnu, known for his conflict with Rāma and for exterminating Kshatriyas.

Dandaka.description: A vast forest where Rāma spends part of his exile.

Janasthāna.description: A region in the Dandaka forest.

Sthana.description: A term related to musical notes or positions.

Murchhana.description: A term related to musical scales or modes.

Mahārathas.description: Great chariot-warriors, a title for elite fighters.

Kāmvoja.description: A region famous for its horses.

Vāhlika.description: A region known for its horses.

Sindhu.description: A river and region, the Indus.

Airavata.description: Indra's divine elephant, the mythological mount of Indra, king of the gods.

Sâmas.description: Sacred chants from the Sāma Veda.

Yupas.description: Sacrificial posts used in Vedic rituals.

Vilwa.description: A type of wood used for sacrificial posts.

catechu.description: A type of wood used for sacrificial posts.

Palasa.description: A type of wood used for sacrificial posts.

Sleshmataka.description: A type of wood used for sacrificial posts.

Devadaru.description: A type of wood used for sacrificial posts.

Garura.description: The divine eagle, vehicle of Vishnu.

Hotâs.description: Priests who recite the Rig Veda during sacrifices.

Adhwaryus.description: Priests who perform the physical aspects of Vedic rituals.

Uâgatas.description: Priests who sing the Sāma Veda during rituals.

Mahishi.description: Chief queen or consort in a ritual context.

Parivriti.description: A secondary consort in a ritual context.

Plaksha.description: A type of tree, used for ritual implements.

Jyotishtoma.description: A Vedic ritual for attaining heaven.

Ayushtoma.description: A Vedic ritual for long life.

Sayambhu.description: A name for Brahmā, the self-born creator.

lacs.description: A unit meaning one hundred thousand.

Atharva Veda.description: One of the four Vedas, containing hymns and rituals.

Siddhas.description: Semi-divine beings known for their spiritual accomplishments.

Vinatā.description: Mother of Garura, the divine eagle.

Pāyasa.description: A divine, sweet rice pudding given as a boon.

Pampā.description: A sacred lake or river associated with Hanumān.

Rishyamukha.description: A mountain where Sugriva takes refuge.

Maināka.description: A mountain that assists Hanumān during his leap to Lankā.

Trijata.description: A Rākshasi who befriends Sita in Lankā; also a Brāhmana of the Garga lineage, recipient of Rāma's charity.

Asoka wood.description: A grove in Lankā where Sita is kept.

Kekaya.description: A kingdom, home of Kaikeyi's family.

Yojana.description: An ancient measure of distance, roughly 8-9 miles.

Menā.description: Mother of Gangā and Umā, wife of Himavat.

Uma.description: Another name for the goddess Pārvatī, wife of Shiva.

Kārtikeya.description: Son of Shiva and Parvati, general of the gods.

Kirtikā.description: The Pleiades, foster mothers of Kārtikeya.

Suparna.description: Another name for Garura, the divine bird.

Kapila.description: A sage, incarnation of Vishnu, who burns Sagara's sons.

Bhagiratha.description: A king, descendant of Sagara, who brings the Ganges (also called Bhāgirathi) to earth.

Trisanku.description: A king who seeks to ascend to heaven in his body.

Viçāla.description: A city visited by Rāma and Viçwāmitra.

Diti.description: Mother of the Asuras, rival of Aditi.

Vāsuki.description: The serpent used as a churning rope in the churning of the ocean.

Mandara.description: The mountain used as a churning stick in the churning of the ocean.

Dhanwantari.description: The divine physician who emerges from the churning of the ocean.

Vāruni.description: Daughter of Varuna, goddess of wine.

Uchhaiçravā.description: A divine horse that emerges from the churning of the ocean.

Kaustubha.description: A divine jewel that emerges from the churning of the ocean.

Kusādhwaja.description: Brother of Janaka, king of Sānkāçyā.

Vasishtha.description: A revered sage and royal priest of the Ikshwāku dynasty.

Yudhājit.description: Son of the king of the Kekayas, maternal uncle of Bharata.

Vānaprastha.description: The third stage of life in Hindu tradition, that of the forest-dweller or hermit.

Godana.description: A ritual of gifting cows, especially at auspicious occasions.

Bhaga.description: A Vedic deity associated with fortune.

Phālguna.description: A month in the Hindu lunar calendar.

Maghā.description: A lunar mansion or nakshatra in Hindu astrology.

ascetic.description: A person who practices severe self-discipline and abstention from worldly pleasures, often for religious reasons.

Vaidika.description: Pertaining to the Vedas or Vedic tradition.

boons.description: Blessings or favors granted, often by gods.

installation.description: The formal ceremony of placing someone in a position of authority, such as a king.

hermitage.description: A secluded dwelling or retreat, especially for religious ascetics.

Arghya.description: A ritual offering of water, flowers, or other items to a deity or honored guest.

sloka.description: A verse, especially in classical Sanskrit poetry.

kamandalu.description: A water pot used by ascetics.

maunja.description: A girdle or belt made from sacred grass, worn by ascetics.

vrishi.description: A staff or stick, sometimes used by ascetics.

adumvari.description: A type of seat made from the wood of the adumvara tree.

Swasti.description: A blessing or benediction meaning 'may it be well.'

Mahāratha.description: A great chariot-warrior, an elite fighter.

Angadas.description: Armlets or ornaments worn on the arms.

Nishkas.description: Gold coins or ornaments worn as jewelry.

pravargya.description: A Vedic ritual involving the offering of heated milk.

upasada.description: A Vedic ritual performed before the main sacrifice.

Satrughna.description: Youngest son of Daçarātha and Sumitrā, brother of Lakshmana, Bharata, and Rāma.

Açwapati.description: King of Kekaya, father of Kaikeyi and maternal grandfather of Bharata; he hosts Bharata and Satrughna during their stay in Kekaya.

Indra.description: The King of the gods and a symbol of power, also referred to as Sachi's lord.

Vrihaspati.description: Preceptor of the gods, associated with wisdom.

Sachi.description: Wife of Indra, sometimes referenced as 'Sachi's lord' meaning Indra.

Nahusha.description: A legendary king in Hindu mythology, known for his temporary ascension to king of the gods.

Yayāti.description: A legendary king, known for his story of exchanging his old age with his son.

Sujajna.description: A Brāhmana sage and priest, son of Vasishtha, who received gifts from Rāma.

Chitraratha.description: Charioteer and counsellor of Ayodhyā, recipient of gifts from Rāma.

Mantharā.description: Hump-backed maidservant of Kaikeyi, instigator of Rāma's exile.

Samvara.description: A powerful Asura demon who was an enemy of the gods and fought Daçarātha.

Mlechas.description: Term for non-Vedic, foreign or barbarian peoples.

Arya.description: Noble or Vedic peoples, as opposed to Mlechas.

Yama.description: God of death and justice in Hindu mythology.

Apsarā.description: Celestial nymphs known for their beauty and dance, often associated with the gods.

Rāhu.description: Demons or planetary portents associated with eclipses and swallowing the sun or moon.

Draviras.description: A people or kingdom in southern India.

Sindhus.description: A people or region, the Indus valley.

Shurashtras.description: An ancient region, modern Saurashtra in Gujarat.

Dānavas.description: A class of Asuras, enemies of the gods.

Satvavān.description: The husband of Sāvitri, a prince whose life was saved by his wife's devotion.

Aja.description: Father of Daçarātha, grandfather of Rāma.

Maudgalya.description: A sage and courtier in Ayodhyā.

Atri.description: A great sage whose hermitage Rāma visits.

Anasuyā.description: Wife of Atri, renowned ascetic and benefactor to Sitā.

Chyavana.description: A sage, son of Bhrigu, known for his asceticism and mystical powers.

Bhrigu.description: A Vedic sage, ancestor of Chyavana.

Sukra.description: The preceptor of the Asuras and the deity associated with the planet Venus.

Soma.description: The moon god, also associated with the sacred drink.

Kuvera.description: The god of wealth and king of the Yakshas, also the half-brother of Rāvana.

Sree.description: Lakshmi, goddess of fortune and prosperity.

Kāma.description: The god of love and desire whose influence is strongly felt in the spring.

Chaitra.description: A month in the Hindu lunar calendar, corresponding to March-April.

Yamunā.description: A sacred river in northern India, tributary of the Ganges.

Prayāga.description: The confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā rivers, modern-day Allahabad.

Kālindi.description: Another name for the Yamunā river.

Mandākini.description: A river near Chitrakuta, associated with Rāma's exile.

Mithilā.description: Kingdom ruled by Janaka, father of Sitā.

Vatsas.description: A region or people in ancient India.

Sumeru.description: A mythological sacred mountain, axis mundi in Hindu cosmology.

Kailāsa.description: The sacred mountain abode of Shiva.

Sudharmā.description: The celestial assembly hall of the gods.

Chaitya.description: A sacred tree or shrine, often associated with Buddhist or Hindu worship.

Saraju.description: A river near Ayodhyā, another name for Sarayu.

Vājapeya.description: A Vedic sacrifice, associated with royal power.

Saptarshi.description: The seven great sages in Hindu tradition.

Atiratha.description: A warrior of the highest rank, capable of fighting many opponents simultaneously.

Dakshina.description: A religious offering or fee, often given to priests after a ritual.

Swastivachana.description: A Vedic ritual of auspicious invocation or benediction.

Sarvaushadhi.description: All-healing herbs, used in rituals or medicine.

Pitris.description: The ancestral spirits, honored in Hindu rituals.

Veda.description: The ancient sacred scriptures of Hinduism, foundational texts of Vedic religion.

Prākrit.description: An ancient vernacular language of India, used alongside Sanskrit.

Mantra.description: Sacred utterances, chants, or hymns used in spiritual practice and rituals.

Pinda.description: A ball of rice or food offered to ancestors during funeral rites.

Yapa.description: Repetition or chanting of sacred texts or mantras.

Krosa.description: A unit of distance, about 2 miles.

Rājarshi.description: A royal sage, a king who is also a sage.

Sruti.description: That which is heard; refers to the Vedas.

Smriti.description: That which is remembered; traditional texts derived from the Vedas.

Lokapāla.description: Guardian deity of a direction or region.

Lokapālas.description: The eight guardian deities of the directions.

Siddha.description: A perfected being, often with supernatural powers.

Mandala.description: A circle or sphere of influence; in politics, a group of neighboring states.

Prakriti.description: Constituent elements or natures; in politics, refers to the elements of state.

Swastika.description: A type of boat, or an auspicious symbol.

Payāca.description: A type of rice pudding or sweet dish.

Rasāla.description: A sweet, often mango-based, drink or sauce.

Kusa.description: A type of sacred grass used in Hindu rituals.

Sāla.description: A type of tree (Shorea robusta), often referenced in Indian literature.

Ingudi.description: A type of tree (Balanites aegyptiaca), whose fruit is used in rituals.

Kata section.description: A branch or recension of the Yajur Veda.

Sāma.description: A type of Vedic chant or melody.

Megha.description: A type of drum or cloud; here, likely a drum.

Japa.description: Repetition or chanting of sacred texts or mantras.

Homa.description: A Vedic fire ritual involving offerings to the fire.

Brahmācharya.description: The student stage of life, characterized by celibacy and study.

Sutikshna.description: A sage in the Dandaka forest who welcomes Rāma during his exile.

Agastya's brother.description: The brother of sage Agastya, also an ascetic living in the Dandaka forest.

Rambhā.description: A famous Apsara (celestial nymph) in Hindu mythology.

Māndakarni.description: An ascetic who creates the Panchāpsara tank and marries five Apsarās.

Dharmabhrit.description: An ascetic who explains the story of the Panchāpsara tank to Rāma.

Maharshis.description: A title for great sages or seers of high spiritual accomplishment.

Vaiçyānara.description: An epithet for Agni, the fire god.

Triçira.description: A Rākshasa general with three heads, ally of Khara.

Kumbhakarna.description: Rāvana's giant brother known for his massive appetite and long periods of sleep.

Bibhishana.description: Rāvana's righteous brother who defects to Rāma's side and eventually becomes the king of Lankā.

Ilwala.description: A Rākshasa who, with his brother Vātāpi, kills Brāhmanas by trickery.

Vātāpi.description: A Rākshasa, brother of Ilwala, killed by sage Agastya.

Danu.description: Mother of the Danavas, also refers to the demon class.

Tamrā.description: Mother of various birds, wife of Kaçyapa.

Krodhavasā.description: Mother of various animals, wife of Kaçyapa.

Analā.description: Mother of trees, wife of Kaçyapa.

Kadru.description: Mother of the Nāgas (serpents), wife of Kaçyapa.

Suki.description: Daughter of Tamrā, mother of Vinatā.

Irāvati.description: Daughter of Bhadramadā, mother of Airāvata the elephant.

Garuda.description: The divine eagle and vehicle of Vishnu, known for his enmity with serpents.

Aruna.description: Brother of Garuda, charioteer of the Sun.

Vaiçyas.description: The merchant and agricultural caste in Hindu society.

Sudras.description: The laborer caste in Hindu society.

Akampana.description: A Rākshasa who escapes the slaughter at Janasthāna and informs Rāvana.

Namuchi.description: A demon slain by Indra in Hindu mythology.

Vritra.description: A demon slain by Indra in a great celestial battle.

Nandi.description: The bull attendant and vehicle of Shiva.

Pulastya.description: One of the mind-born sons of Brahmā, ancestor of Rāvana.

Charanas.description: Celestial bards and singers who witness and narrate great events.

Chaitraratha.description: A celestial garden belonging to Kubera.

Sani.description: The planet Saturn, personified as a deity.

Gāyatri.description: A sacred Vedic meter personified as a goddess.

Vasus.description: A group of eight Vedic deities.

Vāyu.description: The deity of wind and the father of Hanumān.

Arundhati.description: The wife of sage Vashishtha and a symbol of marital fidelity and chastity.

Godāvari.description: A major river in southern India, near which Rāma builds his hermitage.

Panchavati.description: A sacred grove on the banks of the Godāvari, where Rāma, Lakshmana, and Sitā reside.

Rishyamuka.description: A mountain where Sugriva and the monkeys reside.

Kavandha.description: A headless Rākshasa encountered and slain by Rāma and Lakshmana in the forest.

Matanga.description: A sage whose hermitage is near Pampā.

Suryya.description: The sun god and father of Sugriva.

Rikshyaraja.description: Father of Sugriva and Vāli, a monkey king.

Lankā.description: The island kingdom ruled by Rāvana, located across the ocean from the Indian mainland.

Vindhya.description: A mountain range in central India, significant in Hindu mythology.

Matanga's wood.description: The forest region associated with sage Matanga.

Saptaparua.description: A type of tree mentioned as growing near Pampā.

Raktachandan.description: Red sandalwood, a sacred and fragrant tree.

Pāmpa.description: Another spelling for Pampā, the lake or river near Rishyamuka.

Vaitarani.description: A mythical river in the underworld, associated with death.

Meru.description: A sacred mountain in Hindu cosmology.

Panchāpsara.description: A tank or pond created by the ascetic Māndakarni, inhabited by five Apsarās.

Pippali.description: A type of long pepper plant, mentioned as growing in the forest.

Darva.description: A type of sacred grass, often used in rituals.

Matanga Sara.description: A sacred part of the Pampā lake associated with sage Matanga.

Asura.description: A class of powerful beings, often considered demons or anti-gods, antagonistic to the Devas.

Brahmacharya.description: A stage of life or practice of celibacy and self-restraint, especially for ascetics.

Parigha.description: A type of heavy club or iron bar used as a weapon.

Nāga.description: A race of divine or semi-divine serpents or serpent deities.

Nārācha.description: A type of iron arrow or dart.

Vajra.description: The thunderbolt weapon, especially of Indra.

Yoga.description: A spiritual discipline or practice aiming at union with the divine.

Agrayana.description: A Vedic festival or ritual associated with the new rice harvest.

Udaka.description: Water, especially as used in funeral rites.

Kārandavas.description: A type of aquatic bird, possibly a coot or duck.

Chakravāka.description: A type of waterfowl, often identified as a ruddy shelduck.

Krauncha.description: A type of crane or water bird; also refers to a pair of birds whose separation inspires Vālmiki's first verse.

Kinnara.description: A mythical being, half-human and half-horse or bird, known for music.

Sthandilaçāyis.description: Ascetics who sleep on bare ground.

Urddhavāsis.description: Ascetics who practice standing upright as penance.

Ardrapattavāsas.description: Ascetics who wear wet bark garments.

Salilāhāras.description: Ascetics who subsist only on water.

Vāyubhaksbas.description: Ascetics who subsist only on air.

Akāçanilayas.description: Ascetics who dwell in the open air.

Kāsa.description: A type of grass, often used for making mats or thatching.

Chandāla.description: A member of a low caste, often associated with untouchability.

Kārandava.description: A type of aquatic bird, possibly a coot or duck.

Tārā.description: The wise wife of Vāli and later Sugriva, known for her counsel.

Angada.description: Son of Vāli and Tārā, a young monkey prince and key warrior in the search for Sitā.

Māyāvi.description: A powerful asura, son of Dunduvi, enemy of Vāli.

Māndhāta.description: An ancient king, ancestor of Rāma, known for upholding dharma.

Sayamprabhā.description: Daughter of Merusāvarni, a female ascetic who helps the monkeys escape the cave.

Virochana.description: A daitya king, father of Bali.

Jambavān.description: The wise and elderly king of the bears, an advisor and leader among the monkey allies.

Neela.description: A monkey chief/general, commander in Sugriva's army.

Mainda.description: A monkey chief, son of Ashvins.

Dwivida.description: A monkey chief, son of Ashvins.

Sushena.description: A monkey chief, father-in-law of Sugriva.

Golava.description: A Gandharva king defeated by Vāli.

Yaksha.description: A class of nature spirits or demigods, sometimes ministers of Sugriva.

Vālakhilya.description: A class of tiny ascetic sages.

Kinnaras.description: Mythical beings, part human, part horse.

Sumitra.description: Mother of Lakshmana and Satrughna, another queen of Daçarātha.

Kishkindhā.description: The monkey kingdom ruled by Vāli and later Sugriva, located in southern India.

Ayodhya.description: The capital city of Kosala, Rāma's birthplace and kingdom.

Malaya.description: A mountain range in southern India.

Kanka.description: A bird of prey; its feathers are used for fletching arrows.

Asoka.description: A flowering tree (Saraca asoca), symbolizing love and desire.

Karnikara.description: A yellow-flowered tree (Pterospermum acerifolium) mentioned in the forest.

Chakrabaka.description: A type of waterfowl, often identified as the ruddy goose or Brahminy duck.

Karandava.description: A kind of waterfowl, often identified as a duck.

Saugandhika.description: A fragrant, celestial lotus or water lily.

Mandāra.description: A celestial tree or mountain; also refers to a mountain used in the churning of the ocean.

Rājasuya.description: A royal consecration sacrifice performed by kings.

Yajur-veda.description: One of the four Vedas, containing sacrificial formulas.

Rig-veda.description: The oldest of the four Vedas, consisting of hymns.

Shyam-veda.description: Likely a reference to the Sāma-veda, the Veda of chants.

Ikshwākus.description: The solar dynasty to which Rāma belongs.

Srābana.description: A month in the Hindu lunar calendar (July-August), marking the start of the rainy season.

Kartika.description: A month in the Hindu lunar calendar (October-November), marking the end of the rainy season.

Bhādra.description: A month in the Hindu calendar (August-September).

Ashara.description: A month in the Hindu calendar (June-July), marking the start of the monsoon.

Mānasa Saravara.description: A sacred lake, often identified with Lake Manasarovar in Tibet.

Trikuta.description: A mountain with three peaks, sometimes identified with the site of Lanka.

Prasrabana.description: A hill near Kishkindhā where Rāma and Lakshmana stay during the rainy season.

Padmachala.description: A mountain, possibly mythical, associated with lotuses.

Mahāruna.description: A mountain mentioned in the search for Sitā.

Bāhlikas.description: An ancient people, possibly in the northwest of India.

Chandrachitras.description: A region or people, possibly mythical.

Uddalakas.description: A type of tree or region.

Avanti.description: An ancient kingdom in central India.

Somagiri.description: A golden mountain in the north.

Pāriyātra.description: A mountain range in western India.

Chakravān.description: A mountain where Viçwakarmā forged Vishnu's discus.

Varāha.description: A mountain, also the boar incarnation of Vishnu.

Prāgjyotisha.description: A city of gold, ruled by the demon Naraka.

Naraka.description: A demon king, ruler of Prāgjyotisha.

Viçwakarmā.description: The divine architect of the gods.

Maya.description: The asura architect, builder of magical structures.
